reviews.title: Great hardware ruined by predatory software tactics
reviews.text:
The controller itself feels solid, but the setup experience is absolute garbage. As soon as you plug it in and download the required app, it automatically enrolls you in a "Backbone+" subscription trial.
I bought a piece of hardware; I didn't ask for a recurring monthly bill. Forcing users into a subscription funnel just to access the basic features of a controller I already paid full price for is scummy and anti-consumer. If you don't stay on top of your phone’s subscription settings, they’ll start charging you the second the trial ends.
The hardware gets 4 stars, but the company’s "opt-out" business model gets 0. I shouldn't have to dodge hidden fees just to play games on my phone. Avoid if you hate being "subscription-trapped.

reviews.title: Works okay, some weird quirks though
reviews.text:
They asked if I wanted to open a support ticket like I haven’t already opened several and been told by their AI that I’m wrong.

Their AI has now replied to this several times, each time insisting I’m the problem. They can’t accept the fact that they made a mistake.

Update 2:

Looks like Backbone responded again, insisting I’m wrong and asking for details. I literally sent them pictures and details over email, but their stupid AI assistant answered and wasn’t helpful. This company does not care about you. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. They don’t even know how their own app works.

Update 1:

Regarding Backbone’s response to this review, they are 100% WRONG. They are claiming something that I tried before writing this review and it DOES NOT WORK. You get a message telling you to message the game’s developer to add controller support, even if it already does. I’ve actually removed one star from my review because of this, and another star because they use AI as their support agent.


Original Review:

It’s nice that you can add games to your library and easily launch them from there. However, it only lets you do this if these apps support controllers (despite having plenty of games listed that are touch only).

Worse is there are several games that have controller support that Backbone says don’t, and won’t let you add them. This makes no sense why they designed it this way. At the very least, it should warn you that the game might not properly support controllers and add it anyway.

reviews.title: The build quality is garbage
reviews.text: Look ima be honest, I absolutely loved the backbone when I got it, I got the PlayStation edition and was always emulating psp, 3ds,n64 games and wayyy more with it, but I’ve barely had my backbone for a month and it’s been handled with pristine care but somehow my d-pad and left joystick are entirely unresponsive today even tho they were working literally 2 1/2 hours prior to me making this comment and on top of that issue ive had issues with the pass through charging that was advertised as well, seriously this gotta be inspected, for something thats supposed to be built with quality and durability in mind, this is not very durable at all.  The rugged-ness of the backbone pro should be universal among all controllers, what you should do to properly market a backbone pro is to just differentiate them with Hall effect joysticks specifically for the pros but make sure the build quality is consistent among all models, for me and other consumers to spend 100$ for a backbone usb-c to only last barely a full month when taken care of is ridiculous, I’ve had flip phones with better build quality. Takes notes or maybe contact Nokia for advice.

reviews.title: Frustrating Trial and Unexpected Charges
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with the Backbone experience. I signed up for their seven-day trial, set up my email, and did everything they asked. But the app kept looping me back to the sign-up screen and pushing me to subscribe again, even after I’d already entered my payment details.
I tried reinstalling the app and even contacted customer support. They couldn’t figure out the problem and assured me they’d cancel my subscription so I wouldn’t be charged. Despite that, I still got charged on Thanksgiving for a service I can’t even access.
To make matters worse, their phone support is just a voicemail that cuts you off before you can leave a proper message. Overall, it’s incredibly frustrating to be charged for something that doesn’t work and to get no real support to fix it.
*Honestly, the product itself might be fine, but with customer support like this, I can’t recommend it. If you can just use a regular Bluetooth controller and a phone holder, do that instead. Even though the Backbone is supposed to be a good product, it doesn’t feel all that comfortable in my hands. And if the support had been better, I might have overlooked these issues. But the frustration just highlights all the negatives. So yeah, that’s my take.

reviews.title: Cancel before the 7 days is up!!! Zero Customization
reviews.text: For a paid subscription, the menu for the backbone app is absolutely miserable. Tiles cannot be removed. Advertising is all over the place. I would like to open the app and see my library, including streaming services like geforce now and xbox. The current menu is like a puzzle poured onto a table with zero vision or planning. I can’t even get the “three months of free apple music” to go away. I can’t even use it yet, it’s there in plan site taking up a whole “row” of the menu. I’d love to be a beta tester for future enhancements because this is unusable. Any developer looking for feedback can clearly see with a simple google search, everyone is suggesting opening the games as one would any other app in the phone. Every post on the internet says to avoid the app altogether. There is so much potential. I started the 7 day trial but now I’ve set a reminder to cancel. Very disappointed.
